headline: Developer proposes clear glass in some stained glass windows at former Williston West Church, 32 Thomas Street, for residential use.
summary: Jeremy Benney, the project's developer, said the church has been vacant for years and only residential use is allowed on the site. The plan keeps most of the stained glass behind new storm windows, replaces some windows with clear glass, and adds skylights on the flat roof. Members asked the applicant to return with a new plan and suggested hiring a window specialist before the next workshop.
decisions: Approved project changes for new construction at briefly orange street, six in favor.
discussion: Thomas Street window replacement: The developer said clear glass is needed for light and fresh air in apartments that are dark now. Members debated whether replacing some windows meets the preservation standards, and whether removed windows should be kept on site.
Clark windows: Members asked whether the windows connected to Clark could be moved to the front of the building.
Reversibility of removed windows: Members said the applicant should show what happens to removed stained glass and whether it could be put back. Some members said enforcing this would be hard.
Public comment on windows: A speaker from a preservation group urged keeping the windows in their original composition, since they could be reused as art.

decision_evidence.quote: This is review of new construction at briefly orange street. The board voted six in favor, not opposed to approve project changes to that.

decision_titles: Project changes for new construction at briefly orange street
